title: Project
description: A government project or initiative. Subclass of schema:Project, so funder, member and parentOrganization are schema.org terms unchanged. Status (is work happening?) and phase (where in its lifecycle?) are separate: a digital service in beta and a bridge under construction are both 'active'. Only @id, @type and name are required, so a publisher with no project-management system can still publish a valid record. Project health, tasks and assignments are out of scope.

description.description: A plain-language summary of what the project is for.

url.description: Where this project's canonical human-readable page lives.

identifier.description: Scheme-qualified identifiers beyond @id, e.g. a capital-budget project number.

status.description: termCode from the `ProjectStatus` code list. Whether work is happening, not where in the lifecycle (see phase) or how well it is going (not modelled).

phase.description: A DefinedTerm from a lifecycle scheme. Any scheme may be used, so the term is referenced by @id rather than enumerated here. schemaGov publishes the `DigitalServicePhase` scheme; a publisher may reference its own. Whether the term belongs to the scheme it claims is checked by the SHACL shapes.

@id.description: Absolute IRI of the phase term.

position.description: Order of the term within its scheme.

inDefinedTermSet.description: The lifecycle scheme this term belongs to.

expectedEndDate.description: When the project is currently planned to finish. endDate is the actual end.

parentOrganization.description: The organization responsible for the project.

member.description: Organizations taking part in the project.

funder.description: Organizations funding the project. Amounts belong in the budget profile.

produces.description: What the project delivers: a service, dataset, application, facility or document. Separate from the project, which can complete while its output stays in operation.

dateModified.description: The date this record was last reported or confirmed as accurate. A project's status, phase and forecast dates are true as of a date, and without one a consumer cannot tell a current record from a stale one. For a record converted from a dated snapshot, the snapshot date.

sourceDataset.description: The `Dataset` this record was published as part of.
